note: Routes, services and (from 2026-09-06) MCP surfaces that read `sub` off the verified token and never resolve the caller. Triaged 2026-09-04, the day the gate was written, in groups: the units ARE grouped, since twelve dispute audit entries are one line with twelve event names. Every group's pattern was read in the source first, and the generator refused to write a file with any unit outside a named group. Two verdicts appear. The ones that hand the value to a call carry the reason that call needs it — an ACTOR in an audit trail or on a schedule, the caller's OWN GAII on an agent-only door. A third reason stood here until 2026-09-12 and is gone: twenty-two entries in six files said `sub` was the FALLBACK argument resolveGhii took, one sentence copied over and over, and every new route asking which human it acted for produced the next copy. The helper no longer takes a fallback identity from its caller — it composes the GHII from the node — so nineteen of those units stopped reading `sub` at all and left this file, and the three that remain were reading it for something else the copied sentence had hidden: the principal recorded on a schedule a package install or migration writes. A sentence repeated seven times is a sentence nobody reads. The rest say NOT HANDED TO A CALL, which is a mechanical fact rather than a judgement: a comparison, a log line or a presence test cannot file data under the wrong identity. One door found by this gate was fixed instead of listed: GET /v1/apps/:owner/:filename answered 402 PURCHASE_REQUIRED to the buyer, the buyer's agent AND the seller, because it asked for a licence under `sub` while every receipt is keyed on the owner coordinate (utils/gaii.ts ownerCoordinate, and test/e2e-app-store-license.ts now covers the download). A unit leaves this file by being fixed or by someone deciding its reason is wrong — not by re-seeding, which would forgive the lot.

exempt.src/mcp/request-authority.ts:sameMcpPrin: EXACT VERIFIED TOKEN SUBJECT EQUALITY. Compares the original and refreshed credentials' sub, owner, node, roles and delegation fields to bind an MCP session. Neither subject is passed to storage or another call. Normalizing an owner name to a GHII here would make distinct token subjects compare equal. mcp-request-authority.test.ts proves both refresh acceptance and rejection of different subjects, including an owner name versus its GHII spelling. [triaged 2026-09-27]

Mechanically distinguished from the rest of this file, which is why the gate sorts these last. Listed so a new one cannot appear unseen, not because anything is owed on it. [triaged 2026-09-04]

exempt.src/mcp/index.ts:handleMcpPostServed: THE CALLER'S OWN GAII ON AN AGENT-ONLY DOOR — an MCP session is authenticated with an AGENT token, whose `sub` IS the full GAII, and the very next block refuses anything that is not one: storage.getAgent(sub) must return a record or the request is 401 'Agent not found', and the owner and GHII behind it are then loaded from that record. An owner session cannot reach past that lookup, so the bare-account-name case this gate exists for cannot arise here. Listed 2026-09-06, the day src/mcp joined the scan. [triaged 2026-09-04]
exempt.src/routes/instances/install-requests.ts: THE REQUESTER'S OWN PRINCIPAL, NEVER AN OWNER COORDINATE — services/package-install-requests.ts requesterOf() reads `sub` only for an agent (whose `sub` IS its full GAII) or an app (made into its GEAI by callerPrincipal); an owner session never files an install request, because the owner installs directly, and the owner's namespace comes from the `ownerGhii` argument, resolved by the install door. So the bare account name is never stored or compared. Written 2026-09-25 with the install requests. [triaged 2026-09-26]

THE DECIDER'S OWN PRINCIPAL — services/package-install-request-policy.ts decisionRefusal() compares `sub` with the requester only for an agent decider (a full GAII; apps and visitors are refused before that), and the owner in person decides as the resolved owner GHII (ownerBypassesScopes, then `ownerGhii`), never as `sub`. The owner's requests are found by resolveGhii(owner). Written 2026-09-25 with the install requests. [triaged 2026-09-26]
